title: Topological Sort
body:
# Topological Sort

Use for directed prerequisites: produce an order in which every edge `u -> v` puts `u` before `v`, or determine that no such order exists. A cycle makes the order impossible.

```python
from collections import deque

def topo_order(num_nodes: int, edges: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
    graph = [[] for _ in range(num_nodes)]
    indegree = [0] * num_nodes
    for before, after in edges:
        graph[before].append(after)
        indegree[after] += 1

    queue = deque(i for i in range(num_nodes) if indegree[i] == 0)
    order = []
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        order.append(node)
        for neighbor in graph[node]:
            indegree[neighbor] -= 1
            if indegree[neighbor] == 0:
                queue.append(neighbor)
    return order if len(order) == num_nodes else []
```

Use a min-heap instead of the queue when the lexicographically smallest valid order is required. For all possible orders, use backtracking over currently zero-indegree nodes. DFS post-order is an alternative, but needs a `visiting` set for cycle detection.
